title: Is the F.A.A. Grounding the First of Many?
excerpt: On The Political Scene Podcast: Recent disruptions to air travel, banking, and other critical systems have raised questions about the reliability of aging technology—and the risks of upgrading it.
content_html:
Recent disruptions to air travel, banking, and other critical systems have raised questions about the reliability of aging technology—and the risks of upgrading it.

November 20, 2026

Listen and subscribe: Apple | Spotify | Wherever You Listen

Sign up to receive our twice-weekly News & Politics newsletter.

The veteran transportation-safety reporter Matthew L. Wald joins Tyler Foggatt to discuss the Federal Aviation Administration’s recent nationwide grounding order, which disrupted more than ten thousand scheduled flights, and what it revealed about the vulnerabilities of the country’s aviation system. They discuss what caused the ground stop, how a seemingly minor equipment upgrade could have such far-reaching consequences, and whether responsibility lies with the Trump Administration’s cuts and disruption of the F.A.A.’s workforce or with previous Administrations’ failures to modernize the aging infrastructure. They also explore the growing role of automation in air travel, including an eight-hundred-and-seventy-five-million-dollar A.I. system being introduced by the F.A.A., and whether such innovations stand to improve aviation or introduce new risks, from user error to cyberattacks. Does this incident, along with a recent series of high-profile outages affecting technology, banking, and national-security systems, point to a growing vulnerability in the infrastructure that people rely on every day?
